title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: MCP spec 2026-07-28 is now 6 days out — the breaking stateless rewrite lands final next Tuesday
bullets.summary: The stateless core (no handshake/session id, any request to any instance, OAuth-aligned auth, formal deprecation policy) plus MCP Apps (server-rendered UI) and the Tasks extension (tasks/get, tasks/update, tasks/cancel) become the ratified spec on Jul 28.
bullets.how: Every MCP server The Construct runs is 6 days from a breaking change; close the migration inventory + hardening checklist this week. Tasks maps directly onto our long-running scan jobs. Load-bearing action, clock tighter than yesterday.

bullets.title: Google ships Gemini 3.6 Flash (Jul 21) — the cheap, high-volume tier gets another refresh
bullets.summary: Google released Gemini 3.6 Flash on Jul 21, continuing the fast/low-cost lane below its Pro reasoning tier and keeping Flash the default in the Gemini app and AI Mode.
bullets.how: Flash is the natural engine for high-volume, low-stakes Construct batch work (bulk classification, first-pass drafts); worth a cost/quality spot-check against our default for the visibility-scan and content-draft jobs, no re-architecture.

bullets.title: Axonius launches an AI Agent + MCP Server for asset intelligence (Jul 21)
bullets.summary: Axonius exposed a hosted MCP server so trusted asset/security context flows into any MCP client, letting teams ask cybersecurity and asset questions in plain English — another enterprise vendor turning its product into agent-callable plumbing.
bullets.how: Thin direct fit for signage, but reinforces the 'every SaaS ships an MCP' thesis PRAGMA sells; treat client SaaS tools as MCP endpoints an agent orchestrates rather than dashboards a human logs into.

bullets.title: Syncfusion ships BoldDesk AI 2.0 with a hosted MCP server for support workflows (Jul 21)
bullets.summary: BoldDesk AI 2.0 adds a hosted MCP server that gives outside AI tools secure, direct access to help-desk/support workflows, so an agent can read tickets and drive support actions without the vendor UI.
bullets.how: A clean PRAGMA / Pulse SaaS-subscription-replacement wedge: if a client's support desk is agent-callable, one Construct support-ops agent can triage, respond, and resolve; log as reference architecture for 'replace [SaaS tool]' plays.

bullets.title: arXiv — 'Effective Strategies for Asynchronous Software Engineering Agents' formalizes how to run background agents
bullets.summary: The paper studies agents that work asynchronously (fire-and-forget, long-running, revisited later) and lays out strategies for task decomposition, checkpointing, and reconciling results from parallel background runs.
bullets.how: The Construct already runs scheduled/background jobs (this Pulse scan, the Harvard and visibility scans); the async-agent strategies are a checklist for making those runs idempotent and self-reconciling, pairing with the Jul-28 Tasks extension.

praxis_lesson: The dominant signal is unchanged but now urgent — the Jul-28 stateless MCP rewrite is six days out, and the same week keeps producing new hosted MCP servers (Axonius, BoldDesk) that prove 'every SaaS becomes agent-callable plumbing.' The disciplined Construct move is to finish the migration + hardening inventory before the spec lands, and to catalog each new domain MCP as a potential PRAGMA SaaS-replacement wedge rather than chasing the frontier-model refresh (Gemini 3.6 Flash) that changes nothing structural.
